problem_description: kvm_arch_flush_shadow_all() returns early when kvm->arch.nested_mmus_size is 0, skipping the trailing kvm_uninit_stage2_mmu(kvm) call for every non-nested VM so the canonical stage-2 MMU is never torn down (and under pKVM guest pages remain shared with EL2).

NULL pointer dereference in kvm_nested_s2_unmap() and kvm_nested_s2_wp(): both functions dereference kvm->arch.mmu.pgt->ia_bits after nested stage-2 page table walks that can drop kvm->mmu_lock, allowing concurrent kvm_arch_flush_shadow_all() teardown to free kvm->arch.mmu.pgt and set it to NULL.

NULL pointer dereference in invalidate_vncr_va(): walks all vCPUs via kvm_for_each_vcpu() and dereferences vcpu->arch.vncr_tlb->valid without checking whether vcpu->arch.vncr_tlb is NULL (when another vCPU has not yet run/onlined).

Use-after-free / data race in kvm_vcpu_init_nested(): reallocates and swaps kvm->arch.nested_mmus with kvrealloc() while holding only config_lock, whereas concurrent readers (get_s2_mmu_nested() / lookup_s2_mmu()) access kvm->arch.nested_mmus under kvm->mmu_lock.

Signedness truncation bug in pgshift_level_to_ttl() / kvm_invalidate_vncr_ipa(): pgshift_level_to_ttl() takes an unsigned u8 level, so when the guest EL2 stage-1 MMU is disabled (vt->wr.level == S1_MMU_DISABLED, negative -127, pgshift unset) it truncates the negative level and triggers BUG() or mis-sizes the VNCR invalidation range.

TOCTOU race between invalidate_vncr() (under kvm->mmu_lock) and this_cpu_reset_vncr_fixmap() / kvm_vcpu_put_hw_mmu() (without mmu_lock): invalidate_vncr() tests vt->cpu != -1 and calls clear_fixmap(vncr_fixmap(vt->cpu)) while vcpu_put concurrently clears the fixmap and sets vt->cpu = -1, risking clear_fixmap(vncr_fixmap(-1)) or hitting BUG_ON(vt->cpu != smp_processor_id()).

Read-only host memory write violation in kvm_translate_vncr() / kvm_map_l1_vncr(): when a VNCR page is faulted in on a read (!write_fault) from a read-only memslot, writable is false, yet vt->wr.pw (guest stage-1 write permission) alone is used to mark the page dirty and map the per-CPU fixmap writable with PAGE_KERNEL.
Early return when !kvm->arch.nested_mmus_size in kvm_nested_s2_flush() skips flushing the canonical stage-2 page tables for non-nested VMs.

Reference count underflow / use-after-free in vgic_its_invalidate_cache(): iterates its->translation_cache with xa_for_each(), calls xa_erase() ignoring its return value, and unconditionally calls vgic_put_irq(kvm, irq), so concurrent cache invalidations drop the cache reference twice for the same irq.

NULL pointer dereference in vgic_its_save_ite(): unconditionally dereferences ite->collection->collection_id, even though unmapping a collection (MAPC with V=0 / vgic_its_free_collection) sets ite->collection = NULL while leaving the ITE in dev->itt_head.

Missing bounds check in vgic_its_restore_dte(): extracts num_eventid_bits (up to 32) from the userspace-supplied DTE Size field without enforcing num_eventid_bits <= VITS_TYPER_IDBITS (unlike vgic_its_cmd_handle_mapd()).

Out-of-bounds guest memory write in vgic_its_save_collection_table(): computes max_size from GITS_BASER but never bounds-checks gpa or collection->collection_id (via vgic_its_check_id) while writing every collection on its->collection_list into the guest collection table.

Logic bug / race in vgic_its_cmd_handle_movall() and update_affinity(): walks every LPI in dist->lpi_xa and calls update_affinity(irq, vcpu2) without verifying under irq->irq_lock that irq->target_vcpu == vcpu1, retargeting all LPIs in the VM instead of only those on source redistributor vcpu1.
Use-after-free in vgic_its_free_collection() because kfree(collection) frees the its_collection while mapped its_ite entries in device->itt_head still retain dangling ite->collection pointers to it.

Missing migration protection in __rhtab_map_lookup_and_delete_batch(): calls rhtab_delete_elem() -> bpf_mem_cache_free_rcu() inside a preemptible loop (holding only rcu_read_lock(), which does not disable migration under CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU) without migrate_disable(), triggering per-CPU allocator BUG/warnings upon CPU migration.

Unsafe NMI-context destructor call in rhtab_delete_elem() / rhtab_map_update_existing() via rhtab_check_and_free_fields(): invokes bpf_obj_free_fields() directly during resizable hashtab delete/update (which can run in NMI context and before RCU grace period) instead of cancelling timers/wq via bpf_obj_cancel_fields() and deferring field destruction to rhtab_mem_dtor.

Use-after-free / timer corruption in rhtab_map_update_elem(): calls check_and_init_map_value() on elements allocated from bpf_mem_cache_alloc(&rhtab->ma), which zeroes special fields (such as embedded bpf_timer / bpf_wq pointers) in recycled elements while previous RCU-pending timer/work state may still exist.

Missing BTF key validation in htab_map_check_btf() and rhtab_map_check_btf(): neither function rejects key-less BTF (btf_type_is_void(key_type)), allowing hash maps with BTF_KIND_VOID keys to be created and causing a NULL pointer dereference when BTF map printing/seq_show reads the key type.

RCU use-after-free in htab_map_free() because delete_all_elements() and bpf_map_area_free(htab->buckets) free the hash buckets and htab without calling synchronize_rcu() while BPF programs or call_rcu() callbacks are still accessing elements.

sizeof-pointer bug in sve_init_header_from_task(): sets inactive-mode header->size = sizeof(header) (8-byte pointer size) instead of sizeof(*header) (16-byte struct user_sve_header), so the header.size == sizeof(header) check in sve_get_common() (where header is a struct value) never matches and exposes registers from the wrong mode.

Wrong task state corruption in sve_set_common(): calls memset(&current->thread.uw.fpsimd_state, 0, ...) instead of zeroing target->thread.uw.fpsimd_state, clobbering the ptracer's own saved FPSIMD registers while leaving the tracee's FPSIMD state unzeroed.

Missing TIF_SVE flag update in sve_set_common() on systems without SME: the switch setting set_tsk_thread_flag(target, TIF_SVE) for ARM64_VEC_SVE is gated behind if (system_supports_sme()), so PTRACE_SETREGSET(NT_ARM_SVE) fails to set TIF_SVE on SVE-only (!SME) systems.
NULL pointer dereference in za_set() because enabling SME ZA state sets TIF_SME without ensuring target->thread.sve_state is allocated.

Interrupt resource leak in idpf_vport_open(): after idpf_vport_intr_init() succeeds, error paths on queue register init and idpf_rx_bufs_init_all() jump to 'goto queues_rel' instead of 'goto intr_deinit', skipping interrupt teardown.

Uncancelled delayed work and PTP leak on error unwind in idpf_init_task(): when vport initialization fails during driver load (IDPF_HR_DRV_LOAD), idpf_init_task() unwinds vports without cancelling adapter->serv_task / adapter->mbx_task or releasing PTP, leading to NULL pointer dereferences / UAF.
Memory leak in idpf_vport_rel(): frees vport via kfree(vport) without freeing vport->rx_ptype_lkup allocated during vport setup.
Interrupt and queue resource leak in idpf_vport_stop() because interrupts are released before disabling queues and deinitializing XDP rxq info.

Use-after-free in qfq_change_class(): when modifying an existing class (existing == true) fails and jumps to destroy_class, qdisc_put(cl->qdisc) and kfree(cl) free the live class while it remains linked in q->clhash and its aggregate.

NULL pointer dereference in qfq_reset_qdisc(): checks 'if (cl->qdisc->q.qlen > 0)' instead of cl_is_active(cl) before calling qfq_deactivate_class(q, cl), which dereferences NULL scheduler state when an inactive class's child qdisc has non-zero qlen.

State corruption / exploit in qfq_deact_rm_from_agg(): relies on 'cl->qdisc->q.qlen > 0' instead of cl_is_active(cl) to decide whether to call qfq_deactivate_class(q, cl), failing to deactivate an active class whose child qlen dropped to 0 (or deactivating an inactive class).
Use-after-free in qfq_delete_class() because qfq_destroy_class(sch, cl) frees cl without removing it from q->clhash under sch_tree_lock(sch) or checking qdisc_class_in_use().

Infinite loop / soft lockup in __kho_unpreserve(): inside 'while (pfn < end_pfn)', if xa_load(&track->orders, order) or xa_load(&physxa->phys_bits, ...) returns NULL, 'continue;' jumps back to the while condition without advancing pfn.

Higher-order page leak in kho_vmalloc_unpreserve_chunk() / kho_vmalloc_free_chunks(): calls __kho_unpreserve(track, pfn, pfn + 1) assuming order-0 pages instead of unpreserving pfn + (1 << kho_vmalloc->order).

Out-of-bounds array read in kho_vmalloc_unpreserve_chunk() and kho_restore_vmalloc(): the loops 'for (int i = 0; chunk->phys[i]; i++)' lack an 'i < ARRAY_SIZE(chunk->phys)' bounds check, reading past the end of chunk->phys when all slots in a chunk are populated.
Higher-order folio size bug in kho_preserve_folio() because kho_scratch_overlap() and __kho_preserve_order() only check/preserve a single PAGE_SIZE instead of accounting for folio_order(folio).

Workqueue and character device leak in gpiolib_cdev_register(): if cdev_device_add() fails, gdev->line_state_wq is leaked without destroy_workqueue(); and if !gc after srcu_dereference, both cdev_device_del() and destroy_workqueue(gdev->line_state_wq) are missed.

File reference leak in lineinfo_changed_notify(): acquires a file reference fp via get_file_active() before kzalloc(sizeof(*ctx), GFP_ATOMIC), and when kzalloc fails returns NOTIFY_DONE without calling fput(fp).
Use-after-free in gpio_chrdev_release() because kfree(cdev) frees cdev before unregistering cdev->device_unregistered_nb and cdev->lineinfo_changed_nb from gdev's notifier chains.
